claims.claim: the rules of Shuter et al. (1980) as applied at Spednic Lake: spawning starts once daily water exceeds 15 °C; the proportion of eggs and fry dying is 1 if the minimum temperature in the following 15 days falls below 10 °C and 3.0 − 0.2·Tmin between 10 and 15 °C
smallmouth growth 0.12·T − 1.7 mm/d at 14.2–25.5 °C, zero below 14.2 °C (Shuter et al. 1980 via Dudley & Trial 2014)

because the ratio of stored energy to basal metabolism rises with body size, small fish die first, and the first-summer growth needed to survive increases northward; Shuter and colleagues argued this alone can explain the northern range limits of smallmouth bass, yellow perch and Eurasian perch (Shuter et al. 1980; Shuter & Post 1990; both abstracts)
the first winter follows the form of Shuter et al. (1980) in days below 10 °C: at a 208-day winter every young smallmouth under 48 mm dies and none over 92 mm
winter survival length criteria Cmax = 0.3375·w + 22.083 and Cmin = 0.1938·w + 7.917 mm, w = days of winter (Shuter et al. 1980)
smallmouth bass swim-up at 9.1 mm (Shuter et al. 1980)

notes: STAND-IN (read as its own source in the pilot; docs/paper/evidence/Dudley_Trial_2014.json, fetched text docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/Dudley_Trial_2014.txt): Dudley & Trial (2014, USGS SIR 2014-5164) print every rule the paper and code take 'from Shuter et al. 1980' and credit them to it — the spawning trigger 15–27 °C with < 150 degree-days above 10 °C (p. 4, PDF p. 12, "fig. 2; Shuter and others, 1980"); the egg-to-rise mortality table, "Data are from Shuter and others (1980)" (Table 1, p. 5, PDF p. 13); the growth table 0.12T − 1.7 at 14.2–25.5 °C (Table 2, same page, same credit); and the winter criteria Cmax = 0.3375WD + 22.083, Cmin = 0.1938WD + 7.917 with p = (Cmax − L)/(Cmax − Cmin) (eqs. 4–6, pp. 5–6, PDF pp. 13–14, "estimated from the duration of the starvation period (Shuter and others, 1980)"). The 9.1 mm is only "an assumed mean size at rise" there, in the paragraph on Shuter's growth models, with no explicit credit, and the definition of winter days as the span between the autumn and spring 10 °C crossings is Dudley & Trial's own. Until the article is read, cite these as "Shuter et al. 1980, as applied by Dudley & Trial 2014" (the paper mostly does) and drop the bare "(Shuter et al. 1980)" for the 9.1 mm in species.js. The abstract (OpenAlex; not enough to confirm) does say that because the ratio of stored energy to basal metabolic rate increases with size, large fish withstand winter starvation better; that two stages are critical (fertilization to leaving the nest, extreme temperatures; the first winter on stored reserves); and that the model "successfully predicted the observed northern limit" — of smallmouth only: the yellow perch and Eurasian perch range limits in §3.6.8 must come from Shuter & Post 1990. 'Kaevats, Sprules & Shuter 2005' in Table 3.6-6 is another entry.
